articles.title: Papa León XIV en Lima: las 12 rutas de su visita, cierres de avenidas, desvíos y tramos en papamóvil
articles.summary: El avión que transportará al Papa aterrizará, aproximadamente, a las 5:30 p.m. del miércoles 11 de noviembre y, luego, se dirigirá a Palacio de Gobierno para reunirse con la presidenta Keiko Fujimori.
articles.body_text: A pocos días del arribo de León XIV al Perú, ya se definieron las vías por las cuales el sumo pontífice recorrerá para asistir a los eventos en los que participará durante su estancia en la capital y el Callao. Se ha determinado que el Papa recorra 12 rutas. El avión que transportará a Robert Prevost aterrizará, aproximadamente, a las 5:30 p.m. del miércoles 11 de noviembre. La comitiva papal se desplazará por las avenidas Faucett, La Marina, Sucre y Brasil. A la altura del colegio Salesiano San Francisco de Sales, se subirá al papamóvil. Todo el desplazamiento del líder de la iglesia católica será vigilado por un helicóptero. Luego, el Papa recorrerá plaza Bolognesi, Paseo Colón, Av. Garcilaso de la Vega, Av. Tacna, y subirá por el jirón Conde de Superunda. En la plaza Mayor recorrerá sus alrededores y entrará a Palacio de Gobierno para reunirse con la presidenta Keiko Fujimori. Su arribo será entre las 6 p.m. y 6:15 p.m. Como medida de seguridad, la Policía ha establecido un área de restricción que comprende la Av. Tacna, Av. Emancipación, Av. Abancay, el jirón Amazonas y la parte trasera de Palacio de Gobierno. El corredor Azul se desviará por la Av. Alfonso Ugarte, mientras que el corredor Morado se desplazará hacia la Av. Huánuco. Tras su reunión con la mandataria, León XIV se trasladará, al promediar las 7:15 p.m., al Gran Teatro Nacional, en San Borja, por lo que se cerrará los accesos a la Av. Aviación. Ante ello, unas 15 rutas de transporte público convencional modificarán sus recorridos por las avenidas Canadá, Guardia Civil, San Borja Norte y La Cultura. Además, la estación La Cultura de la Línea 1 del Metro permanecerá cerrada. Asimismo, los servicios 201, 204, 206 y 209 del corredor Rojo dejarán de realizar paradas en el paradero La Cultura en la av. Aviación Al día siguiente, el 12 de noviembre, el sumo pontífice volverá a realizar un recorrido en papamóvil por los alrededores de la plaza Mayor para acceder a la Catedral de Lima. En su visita al Estadio Nacional, León XIV entrará por el cruce de las avenidas 28 de Julio y Paseo de la República, la calle José Díaz, e ingresará por la tribuna de occidente. Las autoridades han dispuesto los cierres de los accesos vehiculares en la intersección de las avenidas 28 de Julio y la Av. Paseo de la República, así como en Av. Petit Thouars. Su salida será por la tribuna de occidente, tomará la calle José Díaz, Av. Petit Thouars para dirigirse a la Nunciatura Apostólica, ubicada en la avenida Salaverry. Para participar en la misa en la base Las Palmas, a desarrollarse el 16 de noviembre, el Papa ingresará por la avenida Jorge Chávez. A la 1 p.m. se dirigirá al Grupo Aéreo N°8 para despegar rumbo a Roma. Medidas de seguridad La Policía ha establecido tres anillos de seguridad durante los eventos en los que participará el Papa. El primer anillo estará a cargo de agentes de la Dirección de Seguridad del Estado y miembros de la seguridad personal del sumo pontífice. El segundo y tercer anillo será cubierto por el personal policial básico de las diferentes regiones policiales de las ciudades donde el Papa permanecerá, así como por agentes de las unidades especializadas, los cuales serán previamente capacitados y reentrenados. En Lima, se desplegarán 22,464 agentes PNP, quienes brindarán servicio en la zona de los escenarios y se colocarán en las rutas hacia los eventos. En regiones, habrá 14,685 policías. Cerca de 2.000 policías de tránsito estarán a cargo de las rutas, cortes y desvíos en Lima, mientras que 24 vehículos motorizados integrarán la escolta del pontífice, informó el jefe de la Dirección de Tránsito de la Policía Nacional, general Humberto Alvarado López. El uso del papamóvil El desplazamiento del Papa, tras su llegada del Grupo Aéreo N°8, el 11 de noviembre, será en un vehículo cerrado hasta la avenida Brasil por un tema de “tiempo y de seguridad”, indicó monseñor Guillermo Inca Pereda, secretario general adjunto de la Conferencia Episcopal Peruana. Remarcó que, a partir de la Basílica de María Auxiliadora, en la avenida Brasil, el recorrido será en papamóvil hasta su llegada a la plaza Mayor de Lima. Al día siguiente, el sumo pontífice saldrá en un vehículo cerrado de la Nunciatura Apostólica, en Jesús María, y luego se subirá, a la altura del Centro Cívico, en el papamóvil y avanzará por la Av. Garcilaso de la Vega y Tacna. En el Santuario de las Nazarenas se detendrá y hará una breve oración ante el Señor de los Milagros, y luego llegará a la Catedral a través del Jr. Conde de Superunda. Mario Casaretto, gerente de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres de la Municipalidad de Lima, indicó a El Comercio que la Policía colocará vallas altas en los alrededores de los eventos del Papa, mientras que las vallas bajas serán colocadas en el jirón Conde de Superunda y en el contorno de la plaza Mayor. En las grandes avenidas, los agentes policiales realizarán una labor de contención para impedir que personas invadan la vía o impidan el avance de la comitiva papal.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.
articles.body_text: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down. OpenAI did not announce this acquisition, nor confirm it to TechCrunch, when asked. Nor has it announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners. Travel is one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent , it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses. Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on leasing upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025. When a key partnership with Marriott fell through , the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with $143 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values. So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now, with his joining the company. OpenAI has not yet responded to a request for comment. articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
articles.body_text: New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act , New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports. The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations. The state also can bring enforcement actions against companies that fail to register with the new portal, though a spokesperson declined to provide specifics. “Tech moguls tell us that their vision for AI is inevitable,” Governor Kathy Hochul said Tuesday during a press briefing. “They tell us get on board or get left behind… That any collateral damage is worth it as long as we win the race to the AI cliff.” On Tuesday, Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research based at State University of New York’s Binghamton University. The center will independently evaluate the safety, security, and operation of advanced AI systems and work with DIGIT to review companies’ safety frameworks. Hochul first announced the center in January with $55 million in donations and capital. “We’re building a national model for smart, sensible AI regulation, a model that puts communities above corporations and people above powerful technology,” Hochul said. The RAISE Act isn’t the only safety law New York has passed. Last year, the state began enforcing a law that requires AI companion operators to regularly let users know they’re talking to a bot, and to make reasonable efforts to detect suicidal ideation and self-harm. In October, Hochul signed a separate chatbot safety law for minors, restricting behaviors like deceptive human-like interactions, emotionally manipulative or sycophantic responses, and encouragement of behaviors like suicide or disordered eating. That law takes effect June 1, 2027. Other states have also passed similar AI safety and transparency bills to the RAISE Act. California’s SB 53, which took effect in January, mandates that frontier AI labs have in place and publish safety frameworks, enact whistleblower protections, and report critical safety incidents within 15 days. Illinois’ SB 315, which will go into effect at the start of 2027, has similar requirements, plus includes independent safety compliance audits. articles.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.
articles.body_text: As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell. Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million. At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million. However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range. The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares. The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead. After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively. That’s not their share of the company overall. Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller. Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company. Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others. As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built. Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer. articles.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
articles.body_text: Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.” Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June. Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care. While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care. “Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release . Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million. Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports. “At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.” The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027. Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth. The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI is looking to make ChatGPT a more robust consumer discovery engine, and a host of new features seek to empower businesses to help it do that.
articles.body_text: In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses. On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta. Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products. “As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.” In a move that calls to mind Google Analytics , the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics. Businesses will have to verify their profiles through a formal process, although the company did not share specifics of what that process would entail. Benji Shomair, OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, told journalists on Monday that there are “multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets.” OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort , which had even included a “checkout cart” feature. With the integration of business profiles and intelligence, ChatGPT seems to be attempting to become more like Google, which — since the advent of the internet — has been the place where web users go to understand the companies they want to shop at. It remains to be seen whether this initiative will bear better results than the one that sought to make ChatGPT a direct e-commerce hub. articles.title: Pixel Tag, Google's $30 Android-ready answer to Apple's AirTag, is now available | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google's Pixel Tag lets you track lost items with your Android device, similar to Apple's AirTag.
articles.body_text: Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag, the Google Pixel Tag , goes on sale starting Tuesday, allowing Android users to track items like their keys, wallet, or bag using their smartphone’s built-in Find Hub. First announced in August , the $29.99 device takes cues from the AirTag and other lost-item finders by offering connectivity via Bluetooth and ultra-wideband for precision finding. This lets Android device owners, including Pixel Watch wearers, locate their missing items using a combination of visual distance and directional guidance. Plus, the tag has a built-in speaker to play a chime that helps you locate your item if nearby. (Or, if you’ve lost your phone, you can press the button on the Pixel Tag twice to ring it, too.) You can choose between three different levels of loudness in the settings within the Find Hub, with the maximum volume around 80 decibels. Though the Pixel Tag serves the same purpose as an AirTag, Google has opted for a different design. Instead of a small, round device, like Apple’s, the Pixel Tag is slimmer and more elongated. Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1-inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8-inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height). The slimness of the device might make it more appealing for some, particularly if they’re adding the tag to a small item, like a keychain. The device weighs just 0.4 oz, with the battery included. Unlike Apple, Google opted for a physical button you can press on the tag, which makes it more obvious how it’s meant to work. Google didn’t originally say that the Pixel Tag included NFC when it announced the device in August. NFC is used by Apple’s AirTag to aid people who find lost items, as they can tap the side of the tag to launch a webpage that displays the owner’s contact information. Google uses the tap gesture to instead connect the user to the device’s settings. Meanwhile, for lost items that are not nearby, the Pixel Tag relies on Google’s crowdsourced network of over a billion Android devices globally. The network, similar to competitive offerings from Apple and Tile, taps into the connectivity provided by other Android devices, which can identify and share the location of the lost item back to its owner. This location information is displayed on a map inside the Find Hub app. While the person who found the item can’t tap it, as with NFC-enabled devices, Pixel Tags that are put into “Lost” mode will be able to share the owner’s email, number, and a short message so the person who finds the tag can contact you. When the tag comes back into range of the user’s phone, the item is automatically marked as found. The Pixel Tag’s location can also be shared with up to 10 people in the Find Hub app, which could be useful for shared items like the family car keys, which multiple people might rely on. Like AirTag, the Pixel Tag is powered by a user-replaceable coin cell battery (the CR2032), which makes the device reusable for the long term. (Google claims the device has up to one year of battery life to start.)

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.body_text: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said. When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

articles.title: Reddit is turning user conversations into AI-powered product reviews | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Reddit's new AI-powered reviews summarize what users like and dislike about 10,000 products, helping shoppers research purchases ahead of the holidays.
articles.body_text: Shortly after announcing a plan to transition its site to a logged-in experience , Reddit is debuting a feature that could help make it more of a destination for people doing product research via the web. The company on Tuesday introduced “Reddit Reviews,” a feature that organizes conversations about products into dedicated reviews that include the highlights and key takeaways from users across its communities. The company notes that the new experience builds on one of the ways people are already using Reddit: to learn from others what products are really like, and how they fit into their everyday lives. These first-hand accounts and recommendations can help consumers determine whether or not a particular product is right for them. However, given the rise of generative AI and bots, it’s an area that’s also ripe for “astroturfing” — a term that refers to when a brand fakes public support. With Reddit now effectively turning what was casual online research into more of a structured product, it could become a larger target for these types of fake reviews and recommendations than before. To address this, Reddit’s announcement points to its rules and its latest measures to combat automated abuse and spam , as well as its practice involving community moderators, as tools it will use to keep the reviews on the site legit. The Reddit Reviews feature itself taps into AI to organize the conversations people are having where they describe their product experiences. These posts will often see users discussing how a product works for them, or why it fails, or what the trade-offs are that someone should consider before buying. The company has been testing the product reviews feature since February, initially with U.S. users in areas like Electronics, Video Games, and Health & Beauty products. In September, Reddit expanded the test to include the Home & Garden and Fashion & Apparel categories as well. Now, the company says Reddit Reviews is rolling out to all U.S. users on iOS, Android, and web, with an initial selection focused on around 10,000 products. Over time, it will roll out to more categories and expand beyond the U.S. To use the feature, Reddit users can search for a product or category in the app’s search bar or click on a highlighted product name they see in someone’s comment. From there, the user is taken to a screen where important conversations are summarized under a “what people are saying” heading. This will also include a visual breakdown that shows how many of those comments are positive, negative, or mixed, and what sort of things people said they liked or disliked about the item. For instance, a user considering buying an espresso machine might want to know about things like how much counter space it takes up or whether it’s easier for beginners to understand how to use it, says Reddit. Users can then browse the comments, filter them by topic, or click to be taken to the original conversation, where they can ask more questions or get advice. Users can also move from one product review back to the full category to weigh other, similar products that have been discussed to compare their options, the company said. The feature arrives just ahead of the busy holiday shopping season, when people spend a lot more time doing online product research ahead of their bigger purchases. articles.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company could end up being worth a hefty $1.404 trillion if its shares list at the top of the price range, on a fully diluted basis.
articles.body_text: Anthropic intends to push ahead with its IPO despite shakier markets and the broader pullback from AI investing. The Claude-maker said in an updated IPO filing on Tuesday that it would be offering a total of 825 million Class A shares at an estimated price range of $70 to $78 per share. The sale is expected to raise anywhere from $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion. The company could end up being worth a hefty $1.404 trillion if its shares list at the top of the price range, on a fully diluted basis. That would represent a significant jump up from the $965 billion valuation Anthropic reached in a May fundraise , but it’s still lower than the $2 trillion the company was reportedly targeting a couple months ago. Separately, Anthropic said it had struck a deal to privately sell $26 billion of non-voting Class N stock at the IPO price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC. Google and Nvidia are investing $10 billion apiece. All up, Anthropic estimates net proceeds to reach somewhere between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion (the latter if the IPO underwriters exercise their option to buy additional shares). Underwriters, including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, will have the option to buy up to 123.75 million more shares from Anthropic at the IPO price. As a public benefit corporation, the founders hold a Class F share with 50.1% of the voting power. The Long-Term Benefit Trust will also elect a board majority, so Class A buyers will have limited influence. Anthropic intends to start trading on the Nasdaq close to November 19, per reporting from CNBC , under the ticker symbol “ANT.” The company expects up to 20% of the offering to be allocated to retail investors. Anthropic also gave out a few new details in the updated filing. The company said its run-rate revenue reached $81 billion by the end of October, about $10 billion more than at the end of September. Also, the filing now lists how many shares the company’s co-founders expect to sell in the IPO: CEO Dario Amodei, president and chairperson Daniela Amodei, chief compute officer Tom Brown, Anthropic Institute head Jack Clark, chief science officer Jared Kaplan, chief architect Sam McCandlish, and interpretability research lead Christopher Olah are all selling nearly 3.4 million shares each. articles.title: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon-owned Ring is pushing into robotics with the launch of a home security drone and a rolling robot designed to patrol and protect businesses.
articles.body_text: Ring, the Amazon-owned home security company, is launching its own robotics division, with an eye toward automating security at both the home and the office. The company announced Ring Robotics on Tuesday, debuting two new devices that are sure to stir more than a little bit of controversy. The first new device is a home security drone that users will be able to deploy to patrol their domiciles when they’re out. The other item that the company is launching is a roving enterprise security robot, designed for businesses. First, the drone. Ring calls the device a “flying indoor security camera” — which should give you a pretty good idea of what it’s supposed to do and how it’s supposed to work. Ring Drone Cam is designed to fly from room to room, inspecting what is happening in a user’s house and, if there’s trouble, to alert them. It has been built to integrate with Ring’s other home security devices, so, for instance, if a Ring alarm goes off in a particular part of the home (say, the back door), the bot will supposedly fly to that location and investigate. When it’s not in use, the drone stays inactive in a docking bay. The drone shoots video in 2K and it also comes equipped with LED lights so that it can keep watch at night and record video in low light. It can be controlled via Amazon’s Alexa Home Map , and the bot can also be scheduled to patrol the house at specific times — so, if you know you’re going to be out for the night or even on vacation, the drone can keep you apprised of what’s happening while you’re away. Now let’s turn to Ring Rover Cam. Like the drone, this roving robot can be set to patrol specific routes, at specific times, within the user’s business. The robot streams video in continuous 4K, which is viewable via Ring’s mobile app, and a trigger can be set to automatically record if it detects a human. It also comes with a periscope camera, which can be adjusted to see over specific obstacles, and it includes two-way audio — meaning that, should the remote user need to communicate with a person at the store (be that an employee or a burglar), they can speak to them through the robot. Ring says that both devices are powered by the same proprietary AI system, known as AI Pilot. The company says this system leverages “specialized vision models, sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.” Both devices, using this software, are designed to develop a detailed schematic of your house or office purely by exploring the space for themselves, the company says. “Together, it’s like having a guard on patrol who never clocks out,” the company claims of its new devices. “Ring Rover can do a sweep of the floor after close and investigate when sensor trips at 2 a.m. — streaming it all to your phone, wherever you are.” Automated security is one space the tech industry has never quite cracked. In 2021, Amazon launched its own home security robot, known as Astro. Astro, which resembles Ring’s new robot (the company says that it was inspired to create the bot because of “feedback from Amazon Astro customers”), was first announced as a kind of nebulous domestic helper before being repurposed as an enterprise security product. The device never took off, however, and seven months into the robot’s glow-up as a small business security guard, Amazon put the device out to pasture . The Rover is being made available starting on December 16, and it will retail at a whopping $1,000. The drone, meanwhile, won’t launch until next year, on January 27, and will be made available for $270. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.body_text: Affärskvinnan Alice Huang har anklagats för att ha spionerat åt Kina under sin kärleksrelation med Nvidias vd. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Så inleddes ett internet meddelande som vd:n Jensen Huang skickade till Nvidias anställda i söndags. Bekännandet kom efter att flera medier rapporterat om hans kärleksaffär med den kinesiska affärskvinnan Alice Huang. Hon var hög chef för det Singaporebaserade datacenterföretaget Megaspeed och amerikanska underrättelser misstänker att hon rekryterats för att spionera åt Kinas främsta underrättelsetjänst MMS. I samband med att myndigheter började undersöka henne i slutet av 2024 gick hon under jorden. Sedan dess är det ovisst var hon befinner sig. Tidigare i år ska hon ha varit i Kina, uppger två personer som var i kontakt med henne vid tillfället till WSJ. Det är okänt om hon fortfarande har någon roll hos Megaspeed – som fortfarande är ett aktivt företag. Efter att skandalen briserade i förra veckan har flera medier sökt henne utan resultat. Kinas utrikesministerie har dementerat uppgifterna om spionage och kallat anklagelserna för ”förtal och smutskastning”. För runt 20 år sedan var Alice Huang tv-reporter i statliga kinesiska medier, enligt WSJ:s sammanställning. Hon bytte sedan ut journalistiken mot finansen – hos både kinesiska och Londonbaserade företag. 2023 började hon sin karriär hos Megaspeed. Nina Larsson fick kallelse till mammografi redan i augusti, men den brinnande valrörelsen gjorde att hon bokade om tiden till efter den 13 september. Det var en rutinkontroll och hon förväntade sig att få ett digitalt besked om att allt var bra. Hon fick ett fysiskt brev och en kallelse till uppföljande undersökning. Hon berättade inte om brevet för någon eftersom hon ville få svar först, skriver tidningen Femina. Nyligen fyllda 50 år gick hon på det uppföljande läkarbesöket och efter det gick det fort. En cancerläkare och en kontaktsjuksköterska förklarade att de hittat cancer. – Det är tufft. Det är en väldigt allvarlig sjukdom. Samtidigt är prognosen god. Jag försöker balansera båda de här delarna. Inte negligera sjukdomen eller allvaret i den men inte förstora upp problemen eller oron. Det svåraste hittills har, enligt Nina Larsson, varit att dela det tunga sjukdomsbeskedet med familjen. – Att själv komma över och hantera sjukdomsbilden är på många sätt mycket enklare, men att behöva komma med ett sådant besked till sina nära och kära, det har varit det tuffaste. Nu har hon opererat bort den 14 millimeter stora tumören, portvaktskörtlar och den omkringliggande vävnaden och har inte börjat med strålning än. Hon har fått veta att cancern varken är hormonpåverkad eller ärftlig. Hon uppmanar andra kvinnor att se till att gå på mammografiundersökningarna och inte missa tiden. Viltmästaren Linus Larsson berättar i rätten om sin roll i konflikten kring Trolle Ljungby och beskriver tillkomsten av jaktavtalen som fått kritik. Enligt Linus Larsson försämrades godsets styrning efter att grevinnan dog 2017, och greven var missnöjd med brorsonsonen Carl-Fredrik Wachtmeister. Linus Larsson menar att stämningen på godset blev bättre efter att Carl-Fredrik Wachtmeister fick sluta. Förhöret på tisdagen i Kristianstads tingsrätt blev spänt när advokat Peter Danowsky pressade Linus Larsson om sms-kontakter, men domaren avbröt ordväxlingen med kommentaren: ”Det finns en gräns.” Linus Larsson kom som ung jaktelev till Trolle Ljungby på 90-talet. Utvecklingen av godsets rådjursstam var hans viktigaste bedrift. – När jag kom till Trolle Ljungby var man inte så noga, man åkte upp och sköt ett rådjur här och där som man tyckte var stort nog. När jag började följde vi varje bock noga och det tyckte greven var intressant. När grevinnan Alice Trolle-Wachtmeister dog 2017 blev greven ensam och hade svårare att hålla greppet om godset. Då fanns brorsonsonen Carl-Fredrik Wachtmeister redan inne i verksamheten, men enligt Linus Larsson var greven missnöjd med honom. Framför allt moderniseringar som greven inte visste eller inte mindes att han fått information om.

Han tycker att V-ledaren ska kyla ner sig – och att Magdalena Andersson ska ta ett bad. – Jag har noterat att Vänsterpartiet skruvat upp volymen rejält. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I valrörelsen 1985 tyckte Olof Palme (S) att många moderater, och särskilt partiledare Ulf Adelsohn, betedde sig väldigt febrigt. Så Palme uppmanade M-ledaren att hoppa i plurret och ta ett svalkande bad för att kyla ner sig. – Jag har följt de senaste dagarnas turer. Min känsla är att det är många socialdemokrater och deras närstående som har all anledning att ta ett svalkande bad och kyla ner sig lite grann. Det har inte varit helt lätt att hänga med i svängarna, säger justitieministern. – Under närmare 60 dagar har ingenting hänt från S sida. Det har man försäkrat omvärlden om att det är ett uttryck för att det går väldigt bra i processen. Då kan man möjligtvis undra vad de senaste dagarnas larm och ståhej är ett uttryck för. När Magdalena Andersson efterlyste en ny samarbetsanda i svensk politik såg Gunnar Strömmer ett budskap som medborgare uppskattar, om pragmatiskt och brett samarbete för att lösa stora problem och ta tillvara på möjligheter. – Men i helgen svängde hon ju 180 grader och underströk att om det till äventyrs skulle bli en borgerlig minoritetsregering kan S överhuvudtaget inte prata eller förhandla med en sådan regering. Slutsatsen är självklar, tycker Gunnar Strömmer.

articles.body_text: Meghan Markles pappa Thomas Markle misstänks för att ha innehaft en stor mängd barnpornografi, bland annat diabilder, fotografier och böcker. Han förekommer själv tillsammans med barn i delar av det material som beslagtagits av federal polis. Han greps under helgen. Under natten klippte han av sig sin fotboja, rapporterar AP. Nu sitter Thomas Markle häktad i väntan på förhandling. Nyligen berättade Meghan Markle , hertiginna av Sussex, att hon är djupt skakad av det som framkommit om pappan. Flera personer tog sig in i en bostad i Torslanda utanför Göteborg på tisdagsförmiddagen och rånade en man. Det misstänker polisen, rapporterar Göteborgs-Posten . Offret, en man i 25-årsåldern, larmade polisen själv vid 11-tiden efter att rånarna lämnat bostaden. Han uppgav då att gärningsmännen hade tvingat sig in i bostaden, bundit fast honom och sedan stulit ett kassaskåp. – Vi har varit på plats och hört målsäganden och gjort en teknisk undersökning på platsen och även genomfört dörrknackning, säger polisen presstalesperson i Väst, Adam Samara, till GP. Det är oklart hur många gärningsmän det rör sig om. Ingen är i nuläget gripen eller misstänkt. Mälarbron i Södertälje är trasig och har fastnat i uppfällt läge, rapporterar P4 Stockholm . Sedan 21.00 har inte trafik kunnat passera. Det är oklart när bron kommer att fungera som vanligt igen. E4:an, som går över bron, står helt still. Polisen larmades till Östertälje strax efter klockan 20 med anledning av ett misstänkt brott.
